articles.description: Nazira Haji Zada, a lawful permanent resident, conceded to being an "alien terrorist." It marks the first case in the Alien Terrorist Removal Court.
articles.title: Alien Terrorist Removal Court deports legal US resident to Afghanistan in first-ever case

articles.author: David Cox
articles.description: That's a quote from former rugby star Gareth Thomas, who is HIV positive. At the International AIDS Conference in Rio this year, he spoke out about the isolation and discrimination tied to the virus.
articles.title: 'People are still afraid of those three letters': Fighting the stigma of HIV

articles.author: Glen Weldon
articles.description: The Pitt, Hacks, Widow's Bay and Pluribus are leading the Emmy nominations pack this year. Here's who we'll have our fingers crossed for on Monday night.
articles.title: If the Emmys were up to us ...

articles.author: Katheryn Houghton
articles.description: As state governments grapple with how to determine who's sick enough to be excused from new Medicaid work requirements, some families are already struggling with what illnesses guarantee health coverage because of a disability.
articles.title: A cancer survivor hoped to work — then she lost her Medicaid disability coverage

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: President Trump held talks in Dublin with Irish President Catherine Connolly and Ireland's Prime Minister Micheál Martin during a weekend visit centered on a major golf tournament.
articles.title: Trump meets Ireland's leaders before heading to his golf club in Doonbeg

articles.author: Daniel Estrin
articles.description: Leading Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh has documented Israel's occupation of the West Bank since day one. Fearing the occupation might consume his archive, he secretly moved it to Scotland
articles.title: The secret quest to preserve Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh's diaries

articles.author: Joel Rose
articles.description: The cargo plane crash in Miami is raising concerns about the safety culture at 21 Air, one of the carriers that fly for Amazon. Former pilots were sounding alarms even before Sunday's accident.
articles.title: Miami crash raises concerns about the jet's operator, and why it's flying for Amazon

articles.author: Odette Yousef
articles.description: The assassination of far right activist Charlie Kirk opened the floodgates of neighbor-on-neighbor doxing. A year later, the damage to political discourse in the U.S. remains.
articles.title: Neighbor turned on neighbor after Charlie Kirk's killing. Is the divide here to stay?

articles.author: Huo Jingnan
articles.description: Dario Amodei and Sam Altman are the latest to urge caution amid fears the industry is racing too fast to build powerful AI while safety measures lag.
articles.title: Anthropic and OpenAI CEOs call for AI development to slow down, OpenAI to delay IPO

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosts Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and other leaders of the BRICS nations for a summit on trade, investment, and global conflicts.
articles.title: BRICS leaders meet in India as wars and US tensions test the bloc

articles.author: Kim Willsher in Saint-Martin-sur-Ouanne
articles.description:
Once central to rural life, cafe-bistros are closing in the face of depopulation and falling alcohol consumption, but campaigners are seeking new ways forward
It is just past noon on a midweek day, and already every table at Au Bon Acceuil cafe-bistro in the northern Burgundy village of Saint-Martin-sur-Ouanne is taken.
The three-course lunch menu today – including a choice of a hefty chunk of steak with chips or a meaty lasagne – is just €18, but villagers are not only here for the food.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The battle to save the dying heart of rural France: the village bistro

articles.author: Cait Kelly
articles.description:
Follow today’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Andrew Hastie says he “feels sorry” for Barnaby Joyce and that he and One Nation MP David Farley probably have “buyers remorse” after joining the rightwing party.
Hastie has been feuding with Pauline Hanson this week over a One Nation animated cartoon which labelled him a “traitor” after he gave evidence against Ben Roberts-Smith in his failed defamation trial.
If she were to be prime minister, is she going to run cartoons about all her political opponents? How’s she going to devote her time? Is she serious? Does she have a worldview that we can actually understand? These are all legitimate questions for One Nation …
The whole party centres on her. I think this is why Barnaby Joyce and I reckon David Farley are probably having buyer’s remorse. They’re thinking, “what did I get myself into?”
Look, I’ll say this about Barnaby Joyce. I feel sorry for the bloke, all right? He left a party that made him deputy prime minister twice, to jump in with this rabble, there’s no principles, they’re all over the shop, and he’s out there every week cleaning up after them.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: News live: first case of bird flu in endangered Australian sea lion confirmed; WA police hunting for two men after Perth shooting

articles.author: Krishani Dhanji
articles.description:
Andrew Hastie also says One Nation leader is ‘not the person I thought she was’ and he feels sorry for Joyce

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese has labelled Pauline Hanson nasty and spiteful over resurfaced comments from the One Nation leader criticising his mother for living in public housing for decades.
Hanson also faced further a political threat from Liberal MP Andrew Hastie – who vowed to go “all the way” in his fight with her – as he suggested One Nation MPs Barnaby Joyce and David Farley were likely feeling buyers’ remorse for joining the party.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Albanese hits back at Pauline Hanson’s ‘nastiness’ after criticism of his mother’s use of public housing

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Prime minister’s office tells families of those missing ‘the nation stands with you’ as search and rescue efforts continue
One person has died and more than 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu, the country’s government says.
The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail with more than 40 passengers and crew on Friday from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One dead and more than 30 missing after ferry sinks off Vanuatu coast in rough seas

articles.author: Ben Smee
articles.description:
Screen limits will become mandatory in NSW schools from 2028 as federal education minister says students may need a ‘digital detox’

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast


The New South Wales government has announced it will implement limits on screen time in public school classrooms and push for students to take part in daily “pen and paper” learning.
The state’s new regulations follow a similar announcement from the Victorian government and suggestions by the federal education minister, Jason Clare, that students might need a “digital detox”.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NSW to put strict caps on screen time in classrooms while pushing for ‘pen and paper’ learning

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Iran-allied Houthis say drones and missiles used in attack that targeted ‘weapons depots and command and control centres’ in southern Saudi Arabia
Houthi fighters on Sunday said they used drones and missiles to attack a military base in southern Saudi Arabia as renewed fighting with Yemen’s government forces led growing numbers of civilians to flee.
The attack at the southern Sharurah base targeted “weapons depots and command and control centres that are managing the aggression against our nation and people”, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree wrote on X.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Houthis claim attack on Saudi base as fighting flares with Yemeni forces

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
OpenAI’s decision comes after dire warnings about rapidly progressing technology and lawmakers’ calls for new rules
OpenAI will not go public in 2026, Sam Altman said in a Fortune interview published on Saturday, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence.
“I actually think that, given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public, and we don’t feel pressure on that,” Altman, OpenAI’s CEO, told Fortune.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: OpenAI IPO will not happen in 2026 amid AI safety fears, Sam Altman says

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
Molar from large mammal that once lived in North America is in ‘immaculate condition’ after discovery in Bay Area
A 10,000 year-old tooth in remarkable condition from an ancient Pacific mastodon, a large mammal that once inhabited North America, was recently discovered by a California scientist.
Brigid Lynch, a geomorphologist, was working at a preserve in San Mateo county, when she stumbled across a peculiar rock.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fossilized 10,000-year-old mastodon tooth found by California scientist

articles.author: Henry Belot
articles.description:
Exclusive: Strategic rethink urges progressive activists to respectfully steer one-on-one conversations with One Nation supporters towards economic concerns

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The message from strategists was blunt: do not, however tempting, personally attack Pauline Hanson or call her a racist.
The request has been made to progressive campaigners and unionists who have been asked to start one-on-one conversations with One Nation supporters before the Victorian election in November.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Do not call her a racist: anti-Pauline Hanson strategists tell campaigners character attacks won’t work in Victoria

articles.author: Benita Kolovos
articles.description:
Potholed roads are ‘devastating political advertising’ for the Victorian government – but Ben Carroll has made them the focus of his campaign

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

At a press conference to celebrate the sold-out NFL match played at Melbourne’s MCG on Friday, the Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, was heckled on one issue.
“Fix the potholes,” a punter called out as they walked past the Victorian premier’s press conference.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labor has had 12 years to fix Victorian roads. Turning to ‘pothole populism’ now may be too late

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Trump, again trying to curate museum, says exhibit would stay until 2032 for 300th anniversary of Washington’s birth
Donald Trump asked the Smithsonian Institution to install a 30ft “Colossus statue” of George Washington outside the National Museum of American History, and a special exhibit honoring the nation’s first president, in a social media post late on Friday.
The president requested that the exhibit continue through February 2032, the 300th anniversary of Washington’s birth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump asks Smithsonian to install ‘Colossus statue’ of George Washington with exhibit

articles.author: Keely Aouga
articles.description:
Michael Diehl allegedly forged magistrates’ signatures in North Carolina to allow enough time for ICE to take custody of prisoners
A former Guilford county detention officer in North Carolina faces forgery charges in connection to 20 alleged forged Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainment documents, according to a Guilford county sheriff’s office (GCSO) news release.
Guilford county’s sheriff, Danny H Rogers, reported that on Friday the Guilford county magistrate’s office notified the GCSO of a potentially forged court document submitted by GCSO detention officer Michael Diehl, 40.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Former US detention officer charged with 20 counts of felony forgery

articles.author: Sammy Gecsoyler and Raphael Boyd
articles.description:
Rightwing activists faced a heavy police presence and counter-demonstrations  to their march against small boat crossings
Two men and a teenage boy have been arrested in Portsmouth at a far-right protest against immigration.
Far-right activists have gathered in Portsmouth for a second weekend after a small boat with 140 people seeking asylum on board was intercepted last Sunday while heading towards the city.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Portsmouth experiences second weekend of anti-immigration protests

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Officials still investigating death of Tasia Fortune, a Black woman, a day after man’s arrest in relation to killing
Mississippi police said on Saturday they were still investigating the death of Tasia Fortune, a Black woman found hanging from a tree last month, a day after a man was arrested in connection with the killing.
Loved ones also painted a picture of Fortune as a mother, athlete and woman of faith who they hoped would not solely be remembered for her horrific death.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mississippi police say more arrests to come in death of woman found hanging from tree

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Party can boost its campaign power with funds from billionaire backers, but it can also lose support from ordinary Britons
All things being equal, pretty much any political strategist would welcome a £72m war chest; a sum higher than the combined spending of every major party at the 2024 general election. But all things are not equal, and with such a huge amount comes risk.
Reform UK has been vocal in its arguments that two sudden £36m windfalls from billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne merely “levels the playing field” with the bigger parties when it comes to funding.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donations of £72m make Reform’s prospects both rosier and riskier

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
US president says on visit to republic that unification will happen eventually so ‘may as well happen now’
Donald Trump has said he would “love” to see a united Ireland and that it “may as well happen now”.
The US president appeared to endorse the push for constitutional change on the island at the start of a two-day visit to Ireland on Saturday. The unexpected intervention prompted a swift rebuttal from the UK government and Northern Ireland’s unionist leaders.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield and Michael Goodier
articles.description:
Exclusive: Many ‘use community protection as a cover for racist thuggery’, raising concerns about fresh disorder
At least 28 anti-migrant vigilante groups have formed in the UK in the last 18 months, ranging from unauthorised street patrols claiming to protect women and children to groups harassing migrants in France and blocking ports.
From Belfast to the south coast of England, the number of active groups has surged since the summer of 2025, according to analysis by the Guardian, amid widespread concerns over fresh disorder after black-clad vigilantes, many of them wearing balaclavas, blocked roads in Portsmouth and Dover last weekend.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Number of UK anti-migrant vigilante groups surges in last 18 months

articles.author: Oliver Holmes and agencies
articles.description:
Riyadh has increased use of East-West pipeline since start of war on Iran to bypass closure of strait of Hormuz
Saudi Arabia has shut down a critical oil pipeline, accusing militants in Iraq of launching drone attacks on the export route being used to bypass the lockdown of the strait of Hormuz.
The world’s largest ⁠crude oil exporter has increased its use of the 745-mile (1,200km) pipeline running across the Arabian peninsula, which links Abqaiq, near the Gulf, to the port of Yanbu, on the Red Sea, since the US-Israeli war against Iran began.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi Arabia shuts down key oil pipeline, blaming drones from Iraq

articles.author: Reuters in Kampala
articles.description:
Royal guards carry casket through streets of Fort Portal amid row over appointment of Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma
Uganda’s King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, long the world’s youngest monarch, has been buried among the tombs of his royal forebears as ⁠his Tooro kingdom looked to put ⁠a bitter succession battle behind ​it.
Oyo’s appointed successor, the news anchor Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, cast nine coffee berries into the grave at the Karambi Royal Tombs, marking the formal handover of power in the western Ugandan kingdom.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burial of King Oyo takes place in Uganda as news anchor prepares for throne

articles.author: Geraldine McKelvie
articles.description:
Party leader, Nigel Farage, ‘humbled’ by contributions from billionaires as Harborne addresses ‘media speculation’

Analysis: donations of £72m make Reform’s prospects both rosier and riskier

The cryptocurrency tycoon Christopher Harborne has given £36m to Reform UK, matching a donation from fellow billionaire Ben Delo.
The pledges mean Reform has received a cash injection of £72m in just 24 hours. They are jointly the largest donations made to a UK political party and have intensified calls for restrictions on money received from individual donors.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Christopher Harborne matches £36m Reform donation of Ben Delo

articles.author: Taz Ali and Hamish Mackay
articles.description:
This blog is now closed, you can read more on this story here:

Full story: Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland

Reuters has issued a series of alerts on Trump’s latest comments (he is currently meeting with Micheál Martin). Here is what the news agency has reported:
On Iran: War will end very soon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he would ‘love’ to see unified Ireland and ‘it may as well happen now’ as he visits Dublin – as it happened

articles.author: Guardian staff and Associated Press
articles.description:
Alleged members of Black Axe criminal network that swindled US women out of $6m flown from South Africa
Six Nigerian nationals linked to an organized criminal network that allegedly swindled American women out of more than $6m through online romance scams were extradited to the United States on Friday.
South African police confirmed they were to be extradited earlier on Friday, while local news in Africa confirmed that the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, known as the Hawks, facilitated their handover to officials from the US Federal Bureau of Investigation and Secret Service at Cape Town international airport, in collaboration with Interpol South Africa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Six Nigerians extradited to US over $6m online romance scam

articles.author: Andrew Pulver
articles.description:
An outstanding figure in the UK film industry, Thomas was noted for collaborations with directors including Bernardo Bertolucci and David Cronenberg
Jeremy Thomas, the distinguished British producer of films including Sexy Beast, High-Rise and the multi-Oscar-winning The Last Emperor, has died aged 77.
A representative for Thomas said he died on Friday “peacefully, at his country home in Oxfordshire, surrounded by his family and loved ones”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jeremy Thomas, British producer of The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, dies aged 77

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Incident is latest to raise questions over Israel’s ability or willingness to stop violent settlers in occupied territory
An Israeli soldier has shot a Palestinian man, wounding him in the leg, as settlers confronted villagers by grazing livestock on Palestinian-owned land in the town of Faqqua in the occupied West Bank.
Witnesses said a group of settlers had entered the area with their livestock, prompting residents to try to stop them. Israeli forces then intervened and, according to men at the scene, opened fire at residents. One of them shot Qassem Hussam, a Palestinian man in his mid-30s, wounding him in the leg.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: IDF soldier filmed shooting Palestinian in leg amid West Bank settler standoff

articles.author: Oliver Holmes
articles.description:
Chinese president’s arrival in Delhi seen as step towards reconciliation after deadly 2020 military clash
The Chinese president, Xi Jinping, has received a red-carpet welcome in India for a summit of Brics developing nations, as regional rivals Beijing and Delhi make a public display of thawing relations while quietly competing to lead at a time of shaky US global dominance.
As Xi stepped off the plane, he was walked past an honour guard of Indian soldiers and traditional dancers in colourful dresses. Later on Saturday, he was due to attend a gala dinner for the two-day summit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Xi Jinping gets red carpet at Brics summit amid thaw in India-China relations

articles.author: Miranda Bryant Nordic correspondent
articles.description:
Latest poll shows 0.3-point gap between left and right blocs, with country’s reputation as global champion of human rights said to be at stake
Sweden goes to the polls on Sunday in an extremely close election that could see the far right enter government for the first time if the country’s rightwing parties can form a majority.
Opinion polls show the centre-left opposition alliance ahead, with Magdalena ⁠Andersson of the Social Democrats the favourite to become prime minister again after four years in opposition, but her bloc’s lead has narrowed considerably in the final days of the campaign.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sweden’s extremely close election could see far right enter government

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
The deadly fire had begun in the ferry’s cargo hold, then tore through the ship within seconds
The bodies of passengers killed in a ferry fire off the Philippines arrived at a port near the resort town of Coron, Palawan, on Saturday morning, as the country’s coast guard warned the death toll of 35 would grow.
Tents were being set up to receive 30 bodies brought from the M/V June Aster, which ran aground near the tourist hotspot after a fire erupted on Wednesday evening and tore through the vessel “in seconds”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Death toll from Philippines ferry fire rises to 35, as officials warn toll will grow

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Rampant Yemeni fighters take control of island in narrow point of Bab al-Mandab strait, which Saudi is relying on for oil exports

Why the rapid Houthi advance matters and what’s at stake

Yemen’s rampant Houthi forces have captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait, expanding their control of the narrow waterway, one of the ​world’s vital shipping routes.
The Iran-aligned Houthis took control of the volcanic island after forces allied to the UN-backed, Aden-based government left in the latest of a dramatic series of reverses along Yemen’s west coast in recent days, including the loss of the port city of Mocha on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran’s Houthi allies capture strategic island on vital oil shipping route

articles.author: Oliver Holmes
articles.description:
Global struggle for control of Bab al-Mandab strait threatens to turn Yemen’s on-off conflict into a forever war

Violence erupts in Yemen again: why it matters globally and how it is linked to the US-Iran war


Saudi Arabia shuts down oil pipeline, blaming drones from Iraq

Nearly 50,000 people have fled a sudden advance by Houthi forces in western Yemen, with entire villages emptied and families trapped near frontline fighting with depleting food supplies, according to aid workers.
Civilians in the Middle East’s poorest country have found themselves victims of a global struggle for control over one of the most important shipping routes in the world, which threatens to turn Yemen’s on-off conflict into a forever war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nearly 50,000 Yemeni civilians flee as Houthis advance along Red Sea coast

articles.author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
articles.description:
Many fear chancellor is wrong man for the job at a time when Germany’s defences against far right are crumbling
A cataclysm. A 9.0 earthquake. A five-alarm fire. A bitter rejection of Germany’s joyous reunification three decades ago, and a threat to the democratic postwar order.
Sizing up the repercussions of last weekend’s win for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland party in the former communist state of Saxony-Anhalt, German commentators expressed a sense of doom, panic and helplessness in the political establishment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Firewall compromised: has Friedrich Merz blown ‘democracy’s last shot’?

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The presidential briefing documents were declassified on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks
Several dozen presidential briefing documents declassified on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, detail intelligence that government officials had gathered about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida leading up to the hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and upended American national security.
The documents illustrate security analysts’ tracking of Bin Laden’s movements and support system, as well as concerns about possible threats to US targets. They also detail officials’ understanding of his network in the United States and other countries, including how his operations were financed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CIA releases dozens of presidential daily briefs on Bin Laden and al-Qaida from before 9/11

articles.author: Agence France-Press in Bangkok
articles.description:
Phra Wachirayan Wi arrested alongside woman he was filmed having sex with in latest scandal to hit country’s clergy
Police in Thailand have arrested a senior Buddhist monk on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m intended for his monastery, alongside a suspected female accomplice he was filmed having sex with.
The case is the latest scandal to hit the clergy in the Buddhist-majority country, after a sex and extortion case involving senior monks last year prompted public outrage and calls for greater scrutiny of temple finances.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Buddhist monk arrested in Thailand on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m

articles.author: Karen McVeigh
articles.description:
Her Horizon Fund seeks $100m to stop practice harming 230m women and girls globally  
Frontline activists and leaders in the fight against female genital mutilation, which has affected more than 230 million women and girls worldwide, have welcomed an unprecedented $15.5m (£11.4m) fund aimed at creating “unstoppable momentum” to finally end the practice.
The launch of the fund comes as women’s rights are increasingly under attack and donor funding is in sharp decline, particularly for work led by FGM survivors in local communities. It is thought to be the largest single philanthropic contribution to ending the practice of FGM.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: $15m fund launched to create ‘unstoppable momentum’ to end FGM worldwide

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Canadian PM Mark Carney hosts president in Calgary, where he grew up alongside large Ukrainian community
Canada offered support on Thursday to boost Ukraine’s air defenses and help replenish its drone stocks, as the countries pledged to deepen their alliance during a visit by Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Mark Carney hosted the president of Ukraine in Calgary in the western province of Alberta, where the Canadian prime minister grew up among a large community of people with Ukrainian heritage.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada offers air defense support for Ukraine as Zelenskyy visits

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Family of late King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV reject committee’s choice of cousin and TV presenter as new monarch
A traditional Ugandan kingdom has become engulfed in a bitter succession dispute after the family of a king who recently died rejected the selection of a television news anchor as his successor.
King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who became the world’s youngest reigning monarch when he took the throne in the kingdom of Tooro in 1995 at the age of three, died on 27 August in the US, where he was receiving cancer treatment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Secret son revelation ignites bitter succession dispute in Ugandan kingdom

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Tokyo
articles.description:
The new ‘true-scale’ map shrinks Europe and North America while enlarging Africa – and depicts the disputed Kuril islands as ruled by Moscow
Japan has asked for the revision of a new world map adopted by the UN because it said it made the disputed Kuril islands appear to belong to Russia.
The UN general assembly voted on Friday to adopt the new map, which makes the African continent larger while also shrinking North America and Europe, drawing condemnation from the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japan seeks change to new UN world map over Russia 'misconception'

articles.author: Tora Agarwala
articles.description:
Following six years of talks, Pitt Rivers Museum will return body parts collected by British colonial administrators to north-east India
Anthropologists and community leaders from Nagaland, a remote state in north-eastern India bordering Myanmar, have expressed joy and relief that human remains belonging to their ancestors that had been on display in a British museum for nearly a century are finally being returned.
On Monday, the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford announced that 39 pieces of human remains – including parts of skulls, a finger and a piece of skin with hair – belonging to the Naga tribes, will be returned to Nagaland after six years of negotiation between the community and the museum.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Our forefathers are coming back’: Naga people celebrate after Oxford museum agrees to return remains

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Rubio visits Ecuador and welcomes cooperation after campaign of unilateral strikes on alleged ‘narco-terrorists’
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, gave new clarity on the approach toward combating drug trafficking in Latin American waters, saying the Trump administration was focused on working with allied countries and aligning with their laws but insisted the military would “still blow up ships if need be”.
The public acknowledgment of a shift in US strategy comes a year after Washington began a campaign of unilateral deadly strikes against those it calls “narco-terrorists” operating boats in international waters.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rubio signals shift to working with allies to fight drug trade as latest boat strike kills three

articles.author: Andrew Roth and agencies
articles.description:
Trump administration to seek extra funding from Congress to ‘dismantle’ Los Tiguerones over narcotics trafficking
The US has designated Ecuador’s Los Tiguerones gang, which stormed a television station during a live broadcast in 2024, as a terrorist organisation as the Trump administration expands its campaign against narcotics traffickers it says are destabilising Latin America.
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, made the announcement in Quito, where he met Ecuadorian president Daniel Noboa, one of several rightwing allies of Donald Trump whom Rubio is courting as a security partner during a three-nation tour through Latin America that began on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Notorious Ecuadorian crime gang designated a terrorist group by US

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba announces decision to pull out in post on X, citing tensions over ‘Harry-Meghan nonsense’
Uganda is withdrawing from the Duke of Sussex’s Invictus Games, the country’s military chief has said, out of respect for King Charles amid division over the “Harry-Meghan nonsense”.
Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, son of the Ugandan president, made the surprise announcement in a post on X on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Uganda to withdraw from Invictus Games ‘out of respect for King Charles’, says military chief

articles.author: Natricia Duncan and agencies
articles.description:
Andrew Frederick’s body was found in property he was staying at in Grenada in January
The family of a British father who was found dead in the Caribbean in January is urging authorities in Grenada to work with UK police to uncover the truth about his death.
Andrew Frederick’s body was found in the property he was staying at in Grenada on 4 January. An autopsy, performed in the same week by a privately hired pathologist, concluded that the 47-year-old’s death was a homicide.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Family of British man found dead in Grenada ask local police to work with UK investigators

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Three men are on trial over the death of brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their friend, US citizen Jack Carter Rhoad, in Ensenada
The father of two Australian surfers killed in Mexico two years ago testified in court on Tuesday that his life had been turned into hell, as the high-profile trial continued into its second day.
Three men are charged in the killing of Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33, respectively, and their 30-year-old American friend Jack Carter Rhoad, who were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast in April 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s hell’: father of slain Australian surfers tells Mexico homicide trial about identifying sons’ bodies

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
India’s statistical system once commanded respect, and its data on economic and social indicators was considered rigorous – that appears to have eroded
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
There isn’t much that we Indians agree on these days. GDP numbers are no exception. Last week, India released glowing GDP numbers for the latest quarter – 7.8% growth – higher than the forecast 7%. It sparked a furore.
Subhash Garg, a former finance secretary under Narendra Modi’s government and now a critic, reframed what Modi called a “herculean feat” as mere smoke and mirrors. According to Garg, the government revised last year’s current-price GDP downwards to inflate this year’s number – he believes the real growth is only 2.6%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Trust deficit’: Why India’s economic data has sparked a furore

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Kathmandu
articles.description:
Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions 
Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.
Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Chinese man at Trishuli hydropower project and Nepali woman in Nuwakot found 10 days into rescue operation
Emergency responders have rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal.
The Nepali military said on Saturday a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flash flood disaster

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Group no longer faces voter misconduct case over wrongly marked box after appeals court throws out felony charges
Alaska prosecutors are dropping voter misconduct cases against a group of residents born in American Samoa after a state appeals court threw out felony charges against a woman who wrongly checked a box saying she was a US citizen.
The state’s department of law announced the decision on Friday, after a three-judge court of appeals panel ruled a week earlier that state law requires proof that defendants who erroneously filled out voter registration forms had a “consciousness of wrongdoing” and intended to break the law.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alaska drops cases against American Samoans who checked ‘US citizen’ on voter form

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Trump, again trying to curate museum, says exhibit would stay until 2032 for 300th anniversary of Washington’s birth
Donald Trump asked the Smithsonian Institution to install a 30ft “Colossus statue” of George Washington outside the National Museum of American History, and a special exhibit honoring the nation’s first president, in a social media post late on Friday.
The president requested that the exhibit continue through February 2032, the 300th anniversary of Washington’s birth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump asks Smithsonian to install ‘Colossus statue’ of George Washington with exhibit

articles.author: Taz Ali and Hamish Mackay
articles.description:
This blog is now closed, you can read more on this story here:

Full story: Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland

Reuters has issued a series of alerts on Trump’s latest comments (he is currently meeting with Micheál Martin). Here is what the news agency has reported:
On Iran: War will end very soon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he would ‘love’ to see unified Ireland and ‘it may as well happen now’ as he visits Dublin – as it happened

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Lutnick said $500bn of estimated $1tn needed to fund checks to all US adults could come from new visa program
Donald Trump’s controversial proposal to give a $5,000 “dividend” to all US adults if Republicans maintain control of Congress in November’s elections would not be paid out from US tax revenues, according to the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick.
“It’s not tax money,” Lutnick said in an interview with NBC News, adding that the administration could “earn the money that Donald Trump wants to pay out, not from the deficit and not from taxpayers”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Taxes wouldn’t fund $5,000 Trump ‘dividend’ if Republicans win midterms, says commerce secretary

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Crowd member repeatedly said some Democrats ‘should be shot’ during Ted Cruz’s speech, without senator responding
On the night Republicans gathered to mourn the killing of Charlie Kirk and warn against the dangers of violent rhetoric, a crowd at the party’s irregular midterm convention in Dallas repeatedly called for a sitting Senate candidate to be shot, while the Republican senator at the podium never denounced or even noted the outbursts.
The outbursts came repeatedly during Ted Cruz’s Thursday night address at the American Airlines center, when he named a Democrat he accused of holding radical views. After the senator mentioned the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani, video footage depicts at least one audience member shouting: “He should be shot!” The same cry followed when Cruz named Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and again after he named Texas Senate candidate James Talarico. Cruz did not pause or respond to the shouting, and it remains unclear whether he heard it from the stage. Cruz did not respond to a request for comment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Calls for Democrats to be shot go unchallenged at Republican convention

articles.author: Jameel Jaffer
articles.description:
Over the past quarter-century, the US supreme court has repeatedly failed to protect first amendment rights. We are suffering the consequences
Congress ratified the first amendment in 1791 but the supreme court didn’t breathe life into it until after the first world war, when prosecutions of antiwar protesters led the justices Oliver Wendell Holmes and Louis Brandeis – and then, fortunately, other justices as well – to realize that US democracy would be undermined, not strengthened, by allowing the government to suppress disfavored political opinions.
Repression during the cold war led the court to better protect the freedom of association, and government efforts to cover up official ineptitude and criminality during the Vietnam war spurred the court to better protect the freedom of the press. It took time, but in each of these instances the court responded to wartime repression by developing new legal doctrine that more robustly protected first amendment freedoms.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The ‘war on terror’ weakened the first amendment. Now we desperately need it | Jameel Jaffer

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Matthew Klimow recalls the day a hijacked airliner crashed into the headquarters of the US defence department in Arlington, Virginia
“All day I had been a good soldier: stolid, resolute, unemotional, rational, and dispassionate,” writes Matthew Klimow, recalling the wave of emotion that overwhelmed him as he arrived home from the Pentagon on 11 September 2001. There was sadness for the lives lost. But there was another emotion, too: humiliation.
“We, as a nation, had been humbled,” writes the retired army colonel, who remained at the Pentagon even after it was struck by a hijacked airliner, killing all 64 people onboard and 125 inside the building. “The fighting force of which I was part had been impotent, unable to protect our fellow citizens. The darkness I felt matched the darkness inside my house as I opened the door.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: He was at his desk at the Pentagon on 9/11. As the chaos unfolded, he refused to leave

articles.author: Simon Jenkins
articles.description:
The US president is ever more wayward – and has little interest in defending Europe. The constitution may hold him to account, but we can’t wait
If Americans vote for a Republican majority in both houses of Congress in November, “I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000.” But they must not spend it in Canada or China or anywhere else outside the US. So said Donald Trump in Texas on Wednesday in advance of the forthcoming midterm elections. He further told voters to “Pretend that I’m on the ballot”. It was a climactic moment in an almost two-hour rant.
Trump does not have the required trillion dollars in his pocket, and it would be illegal to disperse such a sum without congressional approval. In any case, JD Vance now appears to have rowed back on the promise.
Simon Jenkins is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wake up, Britain: Donald Trump’s US is no friend of ours. We must secure our own place in the world  | Simon Jenkins

articles.author: Presented by Jenna Amatulli , with Rachel Leingang , produced by Nada Smiljanic and John Rogers. The executive producer was Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
Donald Trump has thrown a convention to amp up the Republican base ahead of the midterm elections, but not everyone is thrilled about it. Dozens of officials running for re-election have stayed away, choosing instead to campaign locally. Are they worried about Trump’s current unpopularity weighing down their ticket?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump-a-palooza: why are Republicans avoiding the president? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
The world’s most powerful country responded to the worst terrorist attack in its history by inflicting terror of its own – around the world, and at home
As clear as that cloudless September morning, Jenna Jacobs McPartland remembers the moment everything changed. “I was cleaning the bathroom and watching the Today show in the background and nine months pregnant,” the 52-year-old recalls by phone. “I think they were showing ‘Today throws a wedding’ when the news broke in.”
A plane had hit the north tower of the World Trade Center in New York. McPartland did not know that her husband, Ariel Jacobs, was attending a conference at its Windows on the World restaurant. “I called his office to say, ‘Hey, turn on the TV. Do you guys know what’s going on?’ His assistant said, ‘Oh my God, Jenna, he’s there.’ The whole world disappeared and there was this sort of hollow collapsing feeling.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mistakes, mistrust and misdirection: 25 years after 9/11, its dark legacy continues to unfold

articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
articles.description:
The White House posted a photo of bald eagle attacking a Canada goose to send a message – but it was Canada that played a critical role in the recovery of the bird in the US
In late August, the White House posted a real photograph on social media of a bald eagle standing atop the limp neck of a Canada goose.
The raptor presses the goose’s face into the grey winter slush. With its stark white head and brilliant yellow talons, the eagle looks victorious and defiant.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada helped save the bald eagle from near extinction in the US – does the White House know?

articles.author: danah boyd
articles.description:
The very mechanisms that allow the census bureau to resist partisan interference are coming undone. And Congress is silent
When the constitutional architects of the United States got together, they came up with a crazy plan: “What if we count everyone in the country and allocate political representation that way?”
It was a radical act. Until then, censuses had been used by kings to levy taxes and conscript men into war. With the penning of article 1, section 2 of the US constitution, being counted ensured that states would get financial resources and political representatives. Congress was tasked with building the processes to anchor representation to the population. People wanted to be counted. And politicians wanted their people to be counted more.
danah boyd is the Geri Gay professor of communication at Cornell University and the author of Data Are Made, Not Found: A Story of Politics, Power, and the Civil Servants Who Saved the US Census
 Continue reading...
articles.title: American democracy depends on the census. Trump is undermining it | danah boyd

articles.author: Ted Widmer
articles.description:
President suggested US might not help UK if Argentina tried to seize Falklands – a new low for UK-US ‘special relationship’
Last week, Donald Trump suggested in an interview with the British TV channel GB News that he might not help the UK if Argentina tried again to seize the Falkland Islands. It was a new low for UK-US relations.
The “special relationship” (Winston Churchill’s phrase) was never perfect, but the UK helped the US on countless occasions, from Korea to Iraq to Afghanistan. The US often stood by the UK as well – although not during the Suez Crisis of 1956, but Ronald Reagan’s government provided significant intelligence and logistics support to Britain during the dust-up over the Falklands in 1982. That relationship is fading fast.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s comments on the Falkland Islands reflect a fractured US-UK relationship

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright with J Oliver Conroy , produced by Tiara Chiaramonte , engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Jonathan Menjivar
articles.description:
Charlie Kirk's death created a vacuum of power that still consumes the Maga right a year later. Immediately after Kirk was shot and killed, his ultraconservative activist organization Turning Point USA announced that his widow, Erika Kirk, would replace her late husband as CEO. But as Guardian reporter J Oliver Conroy tells Kai Wright, conspiracy theories pushed by Kirk's former allies and proteges have dogged both the organization and Erika Kirk herself. Real questions remain about whether Erika Kirk can maintain the enormous power and influence Turning Point holds on the right and what she is planning to do with the organization. Conroy spent months reporting on Charlie Kirk’s legacy talking to dozens of people within Turning Point USA and the larger Maga movement who view Charlie Kirk as a martyr. Conroy says martyrdom is a powerful force that can’t be controlled


J Oliver Conroy's Guardian story on Charlie Kirk and Turning Point USA:  Grief, fury, conspiracy: inside Turning Point USA after Charlie Kirk’s killing

 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Charlie Kirk's martyrdom fed the right. And then tore it apart – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.description:
Donald Trump pledged to pay every adult citizen in the US a $5,000 dividend if the Republicans retain the House and Senate in the midterms, during a rambling speech at the party's midterm convention in Dallas.
The US president claimed the payment was possible due to the country's 'tremendous economic success, like in history we've never had anything like what's happening'. The  proposal, which would cost more than $1tn, immediately raised ethical concerns


US citizens will receive $5,000 if Republicans win midterms, Trump claims


 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump: we will pay every US citizen $5,000 if Republicans win midterms – video

articles.author: David Smith in Dallas
articles.description:
President’s quest in self-mythology stops off in Dallas for a Republican convention where fans indulged his lies and revelled in his jokes
Kim Il-sung of North Korea reportedly sought transfusions of blood from young men; Mao Zedong of China believed sex with young women could prolong his life; Muammar Gaddafi underwent fat injections and hair transplantation to make himself look younger. But for Donald Trump, the secret of eternal youth lies in nights like this.
The occasion of the Republican midterm convention in Dallas was enough to get the 80-year-old US president’s juices flowing. An arena with thousands of fanatical supporters indulging his lies, laughing at his jokes and burnishing his fantasies of greatness is Trump’s happy place.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: As the midterms loom, Trump returns to his happy place: on stage in the theatre of the absurd

articles.description:
The Canadian province's premier, Doug Ford, installed a billboard-sized sign on the lake's shoreline after the US president signed an executive order on Thursday directing US federal agencies to change the lake's name on US maps, documents and databases to 'Lake America'. Ford told reporters that the lake's name, which is more than 400 years old, would remain unchanged. Trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed last week, with each side ‌blaming the ⁠other for derailing three days of intensive negotiations


Trump signs executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

articles.title: Ontario premier unveils Lake Ontario sign in response to Trump’s ‘Lake America’ order – video

Several hundred anti-immigration protesters faced off with counter-protesters in the centre of Portsmouth on Saturday, as the southern English port city found itself at the heart of Britain’s increasingly acrimonious immigration debate. Under a heavy police presence, approximately 400 protesters marched into the centre of town for a second weekend, chanting slogans hostile to migrants. A similar number of people belonging to anti-racism groups joined them on the opposite side of the city’s Guildhall Square

Portsmouth experiences second weekend of anti-immigration protests

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Thousands of people gathered in Dublin on Saturday to protest against US president Donald Trump’s visit to Ireland. Trump said earlier at a press conference that a unified Ireland would be ‘fantastic’, wading into a complex and politically charged subject during a weekend visit to a major tournament at his Irish golf course. Some of the protesters showed anger over his comment and some said he should not have been invited


Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland

articles.title: Protesters against Trump’s visit to Ireland react to ‘united Ireland’ comments – video

articles.description:
Rightwing activists faced a heavy police presence and counter-demonstrations  to their march against small boat crossings
Two men and a teenage boy have been arrested in Portsmouth at a far-right protest against immigration.
Far-right activists have gathered in Portsmouth for a second weekend after a small boat with 140 people seeking asylum on board was intercepted last Sunday while heading towards the city.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Portsmouth experiences second weekend of anti-immigration protests

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Party can boost its campaign power with funds from billionaire backers, but it can also lose support from ordinary Britons
All things being equal, pretty much any political strategist would welcome a £72m war chest; a sum higher than the combined spending of every major party at the 2024 general election. But all things are not equal, and with such a huge amount comes risk.
Reform UK has been vocal in its arguments that two sudden £36m windfalls from billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne merely “levels the playing field” with the bigger parties when it comes to funding.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donations of £72m make Reform’s prospects both rosier and riskier

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
US president says on visit to republic that unification will happen eventually so ‘may as well happen now’
Donald Trump has said he would “love” to see a united Ireland and that it “may as well happen now”.
The US president appeared to endorse the push for constitutional change on the island at the start of a two-day visit to Ireland on Saturday. The unexpected intervention prompted a swift rebuttal from the UK government and Northern Ireland’s unionist leaders.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield and Michael Goodier
articles.description:
Exclusive: Many ‘use community protection as a cover for racist thuggery’, raising concerns about fresh disorder
At least 28 anti-migrant vigilante groups have formed in the UK in the last 18 months, ranging from unauthorised street patrols claiming to protect women and children to groups harassing migrants in France and blocking ports.
From Belfast to the south coast of England, the number of active groups has surged since the summer of 2025, according to analysis by the Guardian, amid widespread concerns over fresh disorder after black-clad vigilantes, many of them wearing balaclavas, blocked roads in Portsmouth and Dover last weekend.

articles.title: Number of UK anti-migrant vigilante groups surges in last 18 months
